package_info.why_malicious: This package version contains a critical vulnerability (CVE-2018-5968) due to incomplete blacklist protection in its deserialization logic. Attackers can exploit this flaw to supply specially crafted input that bypasses class restrictions, enabling deserialization of dangerous classes and resulting in arbitrary code execution or other malicious actions.

execution_context.file_location: application code using jackson-databind for deserialization

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper();
Object obj = mapper.readValue(untrustedInput, Object.class);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code deserializes untrusted input using ObjectMapper.readValue, allowing attacker-controlled data to be mapped to arbitrary classes due to incomplete blacklist enforcement, which can result in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserializing untrusted input without strict class whitelisting or validation exposes the application to remote code execution, as attackers can craft payloads that instantiate dangerous classes.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, deserialization libraries should enforce strict controls to prevent instantiation of unsafe classes from untrusted data; this version fails to block known dangerous classes, violating secure deserialization practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Deserialization of trusted, validated data sources (such as internal APIs or signed payloads) is legitimate and common in many enterprise applications.
key_indicators: Use of ObjectMapper.readValue on untrusted input
Absence or incomplete implementation of class blacklist/whitelist
Deserialization endpoints exposed to external input

attack_chain.action: Application receives untrusted input and attempts to deserialize it using jackson-databind.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential instantiation of dangerous classes and arbitrary code execution.

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of untrusted data using vulnerable versions of jackson-databind (<=2.0.4)
Lack of class blacklist or whitelist enforcement during deserialization operations
Invocation of ObjectMapper.readValue or similar methods on externally supplied data
file_indicators: Source code patterns where ObjectMapper.readValue is called with untrusted or external input
network_indicators: Unusual outbound network connections or process launches immediately following deserialization of external input
Unexpected remote code execution activity originating from deserialization endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan dependency manifests (pom.xml, build.gradle) for com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind version 2.0.4 or earlier. Review application code for deserialization of untrusted input using ObjectMapper.readValue or similar methods without strict class controls. Monitor for exploit attempts targeting deserialization endpoints and for abnormal process or network activity following deserialization operations.
